newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bid fever drives French stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Bid fever drives French stocks higher.

text.p: French stocks finished sharply higher on Thursday, buoyed by gains in the dollar and bond markets and takeover speculation on the bourse.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.81 points, or 1.34 percent, at 2,248.70, while the CAC-40 December futures contract closed up 25 points at 2,246.
Volume was a heavy seven billion francs, swollen by interest in the French retail and pharmaceutical sectors.
Shares in retailer Carrefour rose 5.03 percent to 3,277 francs after the group said it had raised its stake in the holding company controlling retailer Cora to 41.4 percent.
Carrefour said it bought 8.1 percent of the holding company GMB on top of a 33.3 percent stake purchased last week, fuelling speculation of a creeping takeover.

Oil company Elf Aquitaine said it wanted to find a merger partner for its pharmaceutical and beauty products unit Sanofi. Elf shares finished up 4.54 percent at 455.60 francs, and Sanofi's stock rose 6.24 percent to 494 francs.

The speculative interest in French retail shares has been driven by expectations of a consolidation in the industry on the heels of restrictive legislation making it harder for big suburban stores to expand or open new outlets.
The frenzy in pharmaceuticals has been fuelled by a worldwide consolidation in the industry marked by megamergers among drug companies in Switzerland and the United States.
Signs of slowing U.S. business activity reported by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia helped the bond markets, which expect the report will reduce pressure to increase U.S. interest rates.

But the equities market took the news less cheerfully. "If this news is good for the bond markets, it clearly isn't good for Wall Street because, if it's confirmed, it augurs downgrades in U.S. corporate earnings estimates," a Paris broker said.

Shares in French carmakers fell after the car loan division of Compagnie Bancaire predicted a 10 percent fall in new car sales in France next year. Renault shares closed down 2.99 percent at 107.20 francs after touching a year low of 106.10 francs. Shares in PSA Peugeot Citroen closed down 0.35 percent at 562 francs.
